children: Real estate stocks outperformed the broader markets in October as rotation out of technology stocks benefited the sector, while the Federal Reserve held its rates steady.
The broader AI sector faced a reality check after OpenAI
its annualized revenue expectations downward, triggering heavy investor scrutiny over the sustainability of massive infrastructure capital expenditures.
The Cboe Volatility Index
a four-month high during the month amid circulating market rumors that a major hedge fund had collapsed, reflecting fresh tech struggles.
Persistent technology trade selloff led to major market averages declining in October ahead of the midterm elections.
Meanwhile, President Donald Trump

an executive order this month that aims to reduce the cost of owning a home. The order directs Bill Pulte, the director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to create a pilot program to cancel borrowers' mortgage insurance premiums proactively once the borrowers have satisfied their equity requirements based on current market value.
Furthermore, long-term borrowing costs decreased during the month. The United States 10-Year Bond Yield
fell by 35 basis points to 4.93%. The United States 30-Year Bond Yield
reduced by 32 basis points to 5.31%.
The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) increased 4.98% during the month to 275.07 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF
The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index rose 4.68%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index added 4.58% during the course of the month.
Weekly Winners & Losers
Among largecap stocks, Jones Lang LaSalle
led the gainers, advancing 19.81% to $359.79. The real estate services provider reported a third-quarter earnings beat.
Data center REITs Equinix
(+6.14% W/W to $1,013.70) and Iron Mountain
(+5.99% W/W to $116.55) were gaining ahead of the U.S. midterm elections despite a technology rout this week.
On the election day, voters in 10 U.S. states are set to decide whether to curb data center development in their communities.
Extra Space Storage
followed with a 5.52% addition to $151.32, benefitting from financial results that exceeded analyst expectations, while the full-year core FFO guidance was raised.
CoStar Group
led the losers in the category. The stock fell 11.06% week-over-week to $30.17 after releasing its Q3 financial results and disclosing a deal to acquire Vexcel for $730M.
Sun Communities
lost 5.81% to close the week at $113.26 as Q3 revenue missed analyst estimates.
For the midcap decliners, Compass
(-7.69% W/W to $9.00) led the pack.
The stock's price target was lowered at JPMorgan and UBS. Higher mortgage rates and slowing luxury activity reduce near-term earnings visibility for the company, according to UBS.
Alexandria Real Estate Equities

followed with a 6.56% pull back to $40.20 despite the company turning in stronger-than-expected Q3 earnings and revenue even as its occupancy rate dipped and same-store net operating income slipped from a year ago.
The life sciences campus landlord refined its guidance for the full-year 2026 adjusted FFO per share to $6.38-$6.42, vs. its previous outlook of $6.35-$6.45.
Cushman & Wakefield
led the midcap gainers, adding 12.43% week-over-week to $13.30 ahead of its Q3 earnings release. The company is expected to post an EPS of $0.36 (+22.95% Y/Y) and revenue of $2.79B (+7.11% Y/Y).
For the smallcap stocks, PennyMac Mortgage Investment Trust
(+6.11% W/W to $7.47), Chatham Lodging Trust
(+5.13% W/W to $14.75), Arbor Realty Trust
(-26.71% W/W to $2.14), Farmland Partners
(-17.76% W/W to $8.43), and Medical Properties Trust
(-16.67% W/W to $2.25) were the notable movers.
